clue.text: What's broadcast even parts of vicious self-history (having surprising beginnings)?

definitions.text: What's broadcast even parts of vicious self-history (having surprising beginnings)?

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered, as seed is, so the letters that follow are strewn into a new order
the even-numbered letters of the word vicious, second, fourth and sixth, are taken

explanation.surface: A question about some TV programme that airs the cruel memoirs of its subjects, who get a surprise at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'vicious' are I, I, U; with SELFHISTORY they make fourteen letters to rearrange. The whole clue also describes the programme: a life story broadcast, each episode opening with an ambush of the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running biographical TV show surprised its guest at the outset and then broadcast the story of their life.

clue.text: Knockabout versions of Equus?

definitions.meaning: rough, boisterous fun and rough-and-tumble behaviour
Equus is Peter Shaffer's stage drama about a boy who blinds horses, so a staging of it is a play about horses

explanation.surface: Slapstick productions of Shaffer's famous drama about a stable boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough boisterous fooling is the ordinary sense; split in two, the words give a drama whose subject is the animal Equus is Latin for.

clue.text: Provisional golf tournament bagged by second best

indicators.note: being bagged by something means being put inside it, so the tournament goes within the other pieces

parts.note: to top someone is to best or beat them
the PGA, the Professional Golfers' Association, runs the PGA Championship

explanation.surface: A golf event that is only temporary, won by the player who beat the runner-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used as a temporary measure until a proper replacement arrives is provisional; the answer is used as an adjective here.

clue.text: 18 metal from silvery fish

definitions.meaning: 18-down is EXTRACT, so this means to extract metal from ore by heating it
a small silvery food fish of the salmon family

explanation.surface: Getting metal out of a shiny fish, as if it were an ore.
explanation.walkthrough: The 18 refers to the answer at 18-down, which supplies the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Heating ore to draw out its metal is the verb sense; the noun is a small silvery fish related to the salmon.

clue.text: Bloom in film over lake with mostly irregular covering

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the trimmed word is said to cover the lake, so it is wrapped around it
the trimmed word is said to cover the lake, so it is wrapped around it
mostly means all but the last letter of the word for irregular is kept

parts.note: random means irregular, haphazard
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A flower appearing on screen above a lake, half-hidden by a straggling cover.
explanation.walkthrough: RANDOM loses its M ('mostly') and wraps round L, after O for 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: The film actor known for The Lord of the Rings has this first name, so Bloom in film identifies him.

clue.text: Madwoman's husband in French ensemble with turn-ups at the head and foot

indicators.note: in a down entry a turn-up is a reversal, and at the head it applies to the first two letters only

parts.note: orchestre is the French word for an orchestra, an ensemble of players
the middle letters of the French word for orchestra stay as they are

indicators.note: the foot of a down entry is its bottom, where the last two letters are turned up too

parts.note: the last two letters of the French word for orchestra

explanation.surface: A husband among a French troupe whose trousers have turn-ups, oddly at the top as well as at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light the head is the top and the foot the bottom, so only the end pairs of the French word are turned up; the middle stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jane Eyre, Mr Rochester keeps his insane wife Bertha Mason locked in the attic of Thornfield Hall.

clue.text: Science with endless botanical language upped indication of stress?

indicators.note: in a down entry, upped means the pieces are written from bottom to top, so read backwards
endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: plant names are given in Latin

explanation.surface: Science and botany's endless Latin, raised as a sign of exam stress.
explanation.walkthrough: SCI + LATI, the whole run reversed by 'upped'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type is used in print to emphasise a word, so it is a way of marking stress; the question mark flags the pun on stress.

clue.text: High-flyer in league, leader dropping to knock out United

indicators.note: knock out means a letter is removed
the leading letter of the word league drops down to a lower place in it

parts.note: the leader of league is its first letter
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A star player in the league whose captain is dropped as the side is knocked out of a cup by United.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving L of LEAGUE down gives EAGLUE; removing U leaves the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bird of prey that soars at great heights is a literal flyer high in the sky.

clue.text: Tidal surge in lake (not sea) found in 20?

indicators.note: in places the surge inside the lake's name

parts.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia is really a lake despite its name
a bore is a tidal wave surging up a river such as the Severn

explanation.surface: A tidal wave turning up in a lake, which is no sea, asks where else it might appear.
explanation.walkthrough: The 20 refers to the answer at 20-down, TREETOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Living in trees is what the word describes, so something found up in the branches of the canopy fits.

clue.text: Moan about a gang's outsiders with rough faces

indicators.note: about means going round, so the moan surrounds what follows

parts.note: to cry is to moan or wail

indicators.note: the outside letters of the word gang, its first and last

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; the word gang is used

explanation.surface: Someone complaining about the members of a gang who are outsiders with rough faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugged, rocky and uneven is the sense, used of cliffs and of weathered human features alike.

clue.text: Possible shipping hazard Arctic strait drops in?

indicators.note: drops means the following word is taken out of the strait's name

parts.note: the Bering Strait links the Pacific and the Arctic Ocean

explanation.surface: A query whether an Arctic strait poses a hazard to shipping when something drops in.
explanation.definitionFit: A large floating mass of ice can sink a ship, as the Titanic showed, so it is a possible danger to vessels.

clue.text: Nurse to leave bed in medical drama: it softens the flesh

parts.note: to tend is to nurse or look after

indicators.note: in places the getting-up inside the drama's title

parts.note: ER is the American hospital drama series
to rise is to get up out of bed

explanation.surface: A nurse leaving the bed in a hospital drama, with the line that something softens the flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: A mallet or marinade used in cooking breaks down meat fibres to make the meat less tough.

clue.text: Exhausted by too many curtain calls?

definitions.meaning: worn out, finished, no longer working
an audience that has applauded so long it can clap no more has been worn out by its own clapping

explanation.surface: Actors worn out by having to take bow after bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out and broken-down is the slang sense; taken literally, it is having done all one's applauding.

clue.text: Good neighbour in real life, gent did no wrong

indicators.note: wrong signals the letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A decent neighbour in everyday life, a gentleman who did nothing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The Good Life was a 1970s BBC sitcom about Tom and Barbara Good; Paul Eddington played their neighbour Jerry, so in real life the Goods' neighbour was this actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor Paul Eddington played Jerry Leadbetter, next-door neighbour to the Goods in the sitcom The Good Life.

clue.text: Evidence of good overcome by evil …

indicators.note: being overcome by something means being engulfed by it, so the good is put inside the evil

parts.note: sin is evil or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Proof that virtue has been defeated by wickedness, to be continued in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark or indication that something is present or true is a synonym for evidence.

clue.text: Irregular possibly switching sides at the end?

definitions.text: Irregular possibly switching sides at the end?

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might form another word if rearranged
the final R, for right, swaps sides to become L, for left

explanation.surface: An irregular soldier who perhaps changes allegiance when the war is ending.
explanation.walkthrough: IRREGULAR with its last R (right) switched to L (left) gives IRREGULAL, which is then rearranged. Read whole, a guerrilla is an irregular fighter who may well change sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an irregular fighting band, outside a regular army, is the sense, and such fighters may defect.

clue.text: … the latter side of nature evident in London park?

definitions.meaning: in Stevenson's tale the doctor's evil second self is the latter of the pair Jekyll and his alter ego
the first word of the name of the big royal park in central London

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the darker side of human nature is on display in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 15-across's evil overcoming good.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Hyde is the evil persona of Dr Jekyll, named second in the pair; Hyde Park is the famous London park.

clue.text: Citation in supplementary court

parts.note: extra means additional or supplementary

explanation.surface: A legal reference cited in an additional court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage quoted from a book or document is a quotation, so a citation of a few lines is a synonym.

clue.text: Edward rebuffed by ceremonial-fur-wearing set

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the short name is turned round

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
ermined means trimmed with ermine, the white fur on ceremonial robes

explanation.surface: Edward snubbed by a set of people in fur-trimmed robes, like peers at a state opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a group of people; it is the definition, meaning resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on doing something means being resolved or fixed in purpose, the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Highest branch location to handle surgery by phone?

indicators.note: something heard by phone is only heard, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: to treat is to handle, and an op is surgery, giving a phrase for dealing with an operation

explanation.surface: Where a top branch office is, so as to deal with medical procedures over the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of a tree is where its uppermost boughs grow, so it is the place of the highest branch.

clue.text: Joanna's bits to tickle four men, namely, sons

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals
OR, other ranks, means men as opposed to officers
ie, id est, means namely

explanation.surface: A piano's keys that four men and their sons might play.
explanation.walkthrough: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano (said 'pianna'); tickling the ivories means playing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were traditionally made from elephant tusk, so slang names them after that material.

clue.text: In this TV programme, the bloke's got offers

parts.note: he has, said in a dropped-h Cockney accent as in the programme, becomes 'e 'as
tenders are formal offers or bids

explanation.surface: A comment that in some TV show the man has had offers of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In this TV programme' tells you to speak as its East London characters do, dropping each H, so 'he has' becomes 'e 'as. It is the BBC soap set in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running BBC soap set in a fictional East London borough is the programme the clue points to.

clue.text: An award introducing first of those to go wrong

parts.note: the article gives the letter A

indicators.note: the cup takes in the letter, so it is introduced inside

parts.note: a cup is a trophy or award

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word those

explanation.surface: A prize presented with the first of a group about to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: When a machine or a child misbehaves or malfunctions it is said to start playing up, the same idiom.

clue.text: Singular jazz style that Grappelli could have played

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
trad is traditional jazz, as in British trad of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A unique jazz style that the great jazz violinist might have played.
explanation.walkthrough: Stéphane Grappelli was a French jazz violinist; the answer is short for a Stradivarius violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stradivarius is a prized violin, an instrument a famous jazz violinist could have played on.

clue.text: Fine artist depicting ladies' fingers

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A capable painter portraying women's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The green pod vegetable is also called lady's fingers, a common British name for it.

clue.text: House that used to lead university during commencement

indicators.note: during means within, so the university is placed inside the beginning

parts.note: a start is a commencement or beginning

explanation.surface: A college house that once led the university at its graduation ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' looks like a college residence; it is the royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal dynasty that ruled Scotland and later England was a house that once led the nation.

clue.text: Very form of liberty stopped by Republican

indicators.note: being stopped by something here means being plugged with it, so the R goes inside
a form of a word is a reshaped version, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of freedom blocked by a Republican politician, very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: LIBERTY rearranged to TERIBLY takes R after TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an intensifier, as in awfully good or dreadfully sorry, the adverb means extremely.

clue.text: Kid copied Virgin, beheaded and worshipped

parts.note: to put someone on is to kid or tease them
aped means copied or imitated

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a vestal virgin was a priestess of the Roman goddess Vesta

explanation.surface: A child imitated the Virgin Mary, was beheaded and became venerated, like a martyred saint.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone, treating them as perfect and above criticism, is to revere them as if worshipped.
